                                Shop help

                                Orders inside Nairobi arrive in one to two working days. Orders to other towns take three to five working days. We text you a tracking link as soon as your parcel leaves our shop.

                                Yes. You have 14 days from the day it arrives to send an item back, as long as it is unused and in its box. We refund the money to your PocketPay within three days of getting it.

                                We deliver to Mombasa, Kisumu, Nakuru, Eldoret and most other towns in Kenya. Delivery costs KSh 350 in Nairobi and KSh 600 anywhere else. Orders over KSh 5,000 ship free.

                                At checkout, choose PocketPay and type your phone number. You get a prompt on your phone: enter your PIN to pay. Your order is confirmed in a few seconds.

                                You can change the size, colour or address until we pack it, which is usually within two hours. Open your order and press Edit. After that, call us on 0700 123 456 and we will try to help.

                                Answers that spring open, one at a time.

                                Open a question. The last one closes as the new one springs open, so only one answer is on screen.

                                Veg box help

                                Boxes leave the farm at 6 am on Tuesday and Friday. Inside Nairobi they reach you by noon. We text you when the rider is ten minutes away.

                                Yes. Open your box and press Skip before Monday at 8 pm. You pay nothing for a week you skip.

                                Send us a photo the same day. We take it off your next bill, or add a fresh one to your next box.

                                PocketPay or card. We charge the day before your box leaves, never earlier.

                                                      10

                                                      10 Problem cards

                                                      Three cards, one problem each.

                                                      A clinic asked its patients what goes wrong when they book a visit. Each card holds one answer, and the callout sums them up.

                                                      The queue is long

                                                      You wait two hours in a full room, and you might still not be seen today.

                                                      The phone is always busy

                                                      You call ten times before anyone picks up, and then the slot is gone.

                                                      Nobody reminds you

                                                      You forget the visit, and lose your place for weeks.

                                                      In one sentence

                                                      Book a visit in one minute, wait at home, and get a reminder the day before.

                                                        Fast

                                                        How we'll knowNo surprise fees, ever
                                                      3. 3

                                                        Simple

                                                        Pay in three taps, with PocketPay or a card.

                                                        How we'll knowPaid in under 1 minute
                                                      4. 4

                                                        Calm

                                                        One email per order. No spam after you buy.

                                                        How we'll knowAt most 1 email per order

                                                      16

                                                      16 Data model

                                                      Two kinds of data, kept in two places.

                                                      A data model shows the tables and how they link. This one is for a network of weather stations. Facts that rarely change, like where a station stands, live in Postgres. Readings arrive in a flood, so they live in ClickHouse.

                                                      Diagram DesignA data model: the tables, and the lines show which ones connect.

                                                      17

                                                      17 State machine

                                                      Every alert is always in one state.

                                                      A state machine shows every status one thing can have, and what moves it on. This one is a weather alert: it watches, rises, gets sent, or is missed and tried again.

                                                      Diagram DesignA state machine: each box is a status, and each arrow is the event that changes it.

                                                      Message bus
                                                      The log · newest on the right#1040
                                                      Index#1039

                                                      ClickHouse#1036

                                                      Each helper reads at its own speed. ClickHouse waits and reads in batches, and that is fine.

                                                      NATS JetStream: the shared log

                                                      Every reading lands here first and stays for 48 hours. If a helper breaks, it can restart and catch up by reading the log again. Nothing is lost.

                                                      Database

                                                      Postgres

                                                      Remembers our users, our stations, and who is allowed in.

                                                      Sends each question to the right place, like "how windy is it at the coast?", and answers it.

                                                        export function sendReading(p: Reading) {
- // Old: one topic for everyone, no delivery promise.

+   // Each station writes only to its own topic.
+   const topic = `stations.${p.stationId}.wind`;

                                                      How to read a change
                                                      AAdded. A brand-new file.
